findings.title: Validate native rectangles against independently derived rendered geometry
findings.message: The probe checks native geometry against itself: it takes the rectangle returned by the native query and uses its center to test native hit detection. It never compares that rectangle with the rendered cell's position or dimensions. Consistent errors in scaling, translation, or cell placement can therefore produce passed=true even though native geometry does not match the rendered field.
findings.suggestion: Convert each rendered cell rectangle to screen coordinates independently, account for viewport clipping, and compare the returned screen rectangle against that expected rectangle with a small rounding tolerance. Use an independently derived rendered point for the hit-test assertion as well.
findings.evidence:
point := [2]float64{q.Screen[0] + q.Screen[2]/2, q.Screen[1] + q.Screen[3]/2}
		raw = f.input.QueryProbe(cell.Start, cell.End-cell.Start, point)

findings.title: Clamp horizontal scrolling after text shrinks
findings.message: The scroll offset is bounded below but not by the paragraph's remaining width. After deleting enough text from a horizontally scrolled field, setting visualScroll to the new end-caret X can leave the entire shortened text outside the viewport. For example, an offset of 100 followed by an edit reducing the text to 50 pixels sets the offset to 50, even when the viewport can display all the text.
findings.suggestion: After keeping the caret visible, clamp visualScroll to [0, max(0, paragraphAdvanceWidth - width)]. Derive paragraphAdvanceWidth from the interaction cells' rightmost advance edge rather than glyph ink bounds.

findings.title: Refresh edited layout before pointer hit-testing
findings.message: Pointer hit-testing consults renderAll without refreshing it after a queued edit. Invalidating visualGeometry alone does not help: interactionGeometry rebuilds it from the old renderAll. A pointer event before the next render can therefore select a position from the previous text, potentially beyond the current text length. The new arrow-navigation methods already refresh the layout to handle this event ordering.
findings.suggestion: Call refreshInteractionLayout at the beginning of pixelToCursor, before obtaining interactionGeometry, and test an edit followed by pointer placement with no intervening render.
